# lance-encoding: facade, buffers, configuration and compression

**Retained deep coverage: 38 production files.** This is approximately 60% of the previous production-file inventory, not a requirement to transcribe the remainder. Remaining ordinary files need Module Maps; only selected Key Files may receive new deep records.

[Orientation](../L0-orientation.md) · [File layer](rust-lance-file.md) · [Protobuf schemas](protos.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Behavior](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Scenarios](../L4-crosscutting/scenarios.md) · [Build](../L4-crosscutting/build-and-test.md) · [Cookbook](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md)

## Responsibility and ownership boundaries

The package declares encoders and decoders for the file format; its README describes an internal crate, despite Rust-public modules and APIs. The facade declares a single-file IO trait so encoding need not depend on lance-io. The separate lance-file adapter supplies real FileScheduler integration. Metadata helpers construct protobuf values; they do not write bytes, choose a file version, compress payloads or publish a dataset. (rust/lance-encoding/Cargo.toml:1-12; rust/lance-encoding/README.md:1-6; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-62; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:50-827; rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:17-148)

The crate rejects non-little-endian targets at compile time with the exact diagnostic "Lance encodings only support little-endian systems." The adjacent comment treats broader support as future work requiring testing; this is not a runtime byte-swap option. Private array_encoding and public encodings are distinct module declarations. New feature design must obey the repository's frozen legacy boundary rather than treating the older public helper namespace as an invitation to extend legacy writers. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:11-31; AGENTS.md:15-20)

## IO extension contract and async lifecycle

EncodingsIo requires Debug + Send + Sync. submit_request returns a static boxed future with one Bytes per requested range, including empty ranges. Its priority documentation uses the lowest delivered row to prioritize late indirect reads. The trait itself supplies no scheduler, response-count check, range validation or cancellation policy. Implementations own those obligations. submit_single submits immediately and maps a successful vector to its last element with pop().unwrap(): an empty success panics when polled; surplus results are discarded. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:33-76)

Both optional derivation hooks default to None: bypass for indirect IO and additive per-scope statistics. Their documented fallback is the original service; the default stats implementation creates no recorder wrapper. BufferScheduler inherits these defaults. Its private Bytes owns the backing handle; new moves it into the scheduler. satisfy_request casts u64 endpoints to usize without checked narrowing and delegates to Bytes::slice without a Lance error conversion. submit_request eagerly slices and collects in input order before constructing a ready future, ignores priority, and owns the resulting vector independently of self. Dropping the future cannot undo this already executed work. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:78-134)

The reviewed lance-file implementation splits large ranges, omits physical IO for empty ranges and reinserts empty results; it checks returned chunk count before reassembling. Single chunks clone Bytes handles and multiple chunks copy into a combined allocation. These adapter checks are not checks in the trait or BufferScheduler. The broader FileScheduler queue and cancellation lifecycle remains pending. A contextual decode_batch call creates BufferScheduler from EncodedBatch.data; that partial caller read does not cover the rest of decoding. (rust/lance-file/src/io.rs:39-148; rust/lance-encoding/src/decoder.rs:3412-3440)

## Metadata families and failure boundaries

ProtobufUtils builds the older ArrayEncoding tree; ProtobufUtils21 builds structural CompressiveEncoding and PageLayout trees through a private macro instantiated only with pb21. The pb21 module comment explicitly includes V2.1 and newer. Exact version validation happens separately: V2.1 rejects VariablePackedStruct and has_large_chunk, while V2.2 accepts recursively valid variable fields and requires has_large_chunk on mini-block pages. The constructor has no version argument and cannot establish that acceptance. (rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:19-33; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:50-827; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/reader.rs:99-119; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/reader.rs:99-127)

| Boundary | Exact local behavior and implication | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Older FSL dimension | u64 input narrows to protobuf u32 with try_into().unwrap(); values above u32::MAX panic. Structural items_per_value remains u64. Zero is not rejected by either helper. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:121-130; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:340-356; protos/encodings_v2_0.proto:159-165; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:541-547 |
| Older compression | block stores any string. flat/general use runtime scheme Display and preserve optional level, without checking feature availability. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:93-120; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:221-237; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:112-121 |
| Structural compression | buffer_compression and wrapped return Result. Runtime Lz4 and Zstd convert to protobuf 1 and 2; None and Fsst return InvalidInput. Optional descriptor None is different from attempting to encode CompressionScheme::None. A separate FSST tree variant exists. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:406-477; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:82-95; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:326-330 |
| Layers | Six interpretations map explicitly to codes 1–6; unknown integer codes panic during try_from().unwrap(), and code 0 explicitly panics. No forward fallback is present in this helper. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:479-529; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:54-69 |
| Mini-block | Asserts nonempty interpretations. Copies counts, depth, buffer count and large-chunk flag; None dictionary becomes absent/count 0, Some preserves even count 0. No cross-field validation. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:532-571 |
| Full-zip/blob | Full-zip widens u8 rep/def widths, selects fixed-value or offset Details oneof, and preserves counts. Unlike mini-block, full-zip and blob accept an empty layer slice locally. No visible<=total check. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:573-663 |
| Constant tree versus page | CompressiveEncoding::Constant is distinct from ConstantLayout. Both preserve optional presence. constant_layout clears level streams/counts; compressed_all_null_constant_layout forces absent inline bytes but preserves supplied streams/counts. Neither validates scalar type, inline size, buffers or all-nullness. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:328-338; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:727-770 |
| Packed fields | Structural fixed and variable field helpers choose BitsPerValue or BitsPerLength oneof, retain a present child, and do not derive/check widths. Child order is preserved. | rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:772-826 |

Allocations here consist of protobuf tree boxing, ordered vectors and conversions to Bytes/string metadata; these bodies contain no payload compression loops, IO, async task spawn or global mutable state. Changing oneof arms, child presence/order, width units or count meanings changes what downstream readers interpret. The FSST comment about an ignored older binary child is recorded as author commentary, not a verified statement about every decoder. (rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:50-827; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:195-205)

## Configuration, build and dependencies

Package version/edition/rust-version and lint configuration are inherited. No profile is defined locally. Default features are lz4, zstd and bitpacking, each enabling its optional dependency. protoc enables protobuf-src and is additionally requested for docs.rs. The old-Ubuntu explanation is a checked-in comment, not a current observation of that external service. (rust/lance-encoding/Cargo.toml:1-12; rust/lance-encoding/Cargo.toml:54-85)

The build script emits rerun-if-changed=protos; with protoc, it unsafely sets process PROTOC to the vendored compiler path. No safety explanation of concurrent environment mutation or restoration is present. One prost Config enables proto3 optional syntax, type names and Bytes for all bytes fields, then compiles the V2.0 and V2.1 schemas in order. Errors propagate as std::io::Result; generation is not rolled back if the second compilation fails. format.rs includes the two generated files under OUT_DIR. No build was executed for this KB. ## Exact declarations and local contracts

The following catalog covers all 82 reviewed declarations, including 53 functions. It includes private implementation details because changing them can affect the public contract. Public module declarations do not claim coverage of their child APIs. Macro signatures below substitute the sole pb21 instantiation mechanically; no compiler expansion ran. All exact literal templates remain in the symbol JSON and L2 evidence. Imports resolve as shown in each file's complete appendix. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:4-25; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:35-48; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:307-670)

### lance_encoding::<BufferScheduler as EncodingsIo>

public trait implementation; implementation.

```rust
impl EncodingsIo for BufferScheduler {
```

BufferScheduler submit_request consumes ranges in input order, eagerly slices and collects a Vec before constructing future::ready(Ok(...)). Therefore slicing failure occurs at submission, not first future poll. Priority is ignored; empty input returns an empty Vec; valid empty ranges produce empty slices. Returned static future owns collected Bytes, so it does not borrow self. No IO, backpressure, task spawn, cancellation handling, coalescing, stats override or local tests exist; bypass/stats inherit None. Dropping a returned future releases its results, but cannot undo already performed slicing/collection. (rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:122-134)

### lance_encoding::EncodingsIo

public; trait.

```rust
pub trait EncodingsIo: std::fmt::Debug + Send + Sync {
```

Public EncodingsIo:Debug+Send+Sync supplies a single-file IO service without requiring lance-io. submit_request borrows self, owns Vec<Range<u64>> and u64 priority, and returns a static boxed future of Result<Vec<Bytes>>. Contract requires one returned Bytes per requested range even after coalescing, and an empty buffer for each empty range. Priority should be the lowest row delivered so late indirect reads can be prioritized. Trait declaration does not enforce range legality, response ordering/count, scheduling, cancellation or durability; implementations/callers own those obligations. Default submit_single owns one range/priority, calls submit_request immediately, maps Ok through v.pop().unwrap(), then boxes. Upstream Err is preserved. An empty success vector panics while the mapped future is polled; surplus responses silently drop all but the last. No response-count validation or buffer-size check occurs. Correct one-response implementations return their sole Bytes. Default with_bypass_backpressure returns None. Contract describes a derived IO service for indirect reads to avoid backpressure deadlock/latency; unsupported callers should fall back to self. This default neither clones a service nor changes scheduling. Default with_io_stats accepts Arc<dyn IoStatsRecorder> but ignores/drops it and returns None. Docs describe additive per-scope accounting without reopening files; unsupported callers fall back to self without scope statistics. No counters, wrapper, global accounting or instrumentation are created here. ### lance_encoding::format::<ProtobufUtils>

inherent; implementation.

```rust
impl ProtobufUtils {
```

Imports older protobuf ArrayEncoding/variant types and aliases, Page BufferType, Nullable arms, shared CompressionConfig, DefinitionInterpretation, Constant and Result. Public empty ProtobufUtils is an associated-function namespace; no stored state, constructor requirement, IO or registration. ProtobufUtils::constant moves Vec<u8> into protobuf Bytes and wraps Some(ArrayEncoding::Constant). It does not infer data type, require a nonempty value or validate its width. This older array descriptor is distinct from ConstantLayout pages. basic_all_null_encoding builds Nullable(Some(AllNulls(empty marker))). It has no value/validity children, buffer references or row count; caller supplies those through other metadata. basic_some_null_encoding owns validity and value descriptors, boxes each under Some and wraps Nullable(Some(SomeNulls(...))). ## Configuration, accumulation and buffer compression

The following nine files add 1,697 fully read lines. Coverage of neighboring selection/decoder/harness code remains limited to the cited snippets.

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/constants.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/constants.rs.md): Public string constants for field metadata and environment variable names. Declarations document policy inputs; this file performs no parsing, validation or environment access.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs.md): Public compression policy records, field/type selection, partial merge and private wildcard matcher; four local tests define selected precedence cases.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/utils.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/utils.rs.md): Public utilities facade.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs.md): Public synchronous queue accumulating Arrow arrays into page-sized groups, with optional copying and caller-supplied top-level row accounting.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/bytepack.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/bytepack.rs.md): Fixed-byte-width unsigned integer writer and iterator decoder; zero-width writer is an omission mode, not an encoded integer stream.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings.rs.md): Public logical/physical encoding facade with test-only fuzz module.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical.rs.md): Public logical encoding module declarations.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical.rs.md): Public physical codec module declarations and optional bitpacking module.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs.md): General buffer codec configuration/selection, Zstd and LZ4 framing, append-oriented compression, whole-block and per-value adapters, and local tests.

### Configuration precedence and validation boundary

CompressionParams first merges an exact DataType::to_string key, then either an exact column key or the first matching wildcard entry in HashMap order. An exact empty record suppresses patterns, several matching patterns have no specificity priority, and None cannot clear inherited values. Pattern syntax is one simple prefix/suffix/middle star branch, not general globbing. Field-level parameters carry optional values without validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:45-169)

The reviewed V2.2 strategy then overlays field metadata. Its parser copies compression strings, silently drops invalid numeric level/threshold parses, warns and skips invalid BSS/chunk-size values, and returns partial fields. Thus the comment "using default" on invalid BSS can mean preserving an inherited setting after merge, not necessarily forcing Auto. Full compression selection and version-specific restrictions still require the complete policy files. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:27-38; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:560-591; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:122-141)

Metadata keys and two dictionary-value environment identifiers are literal public constants. They do not read the environment themselves. One contextual dictionary caller reads both env variables and delegates precedence to a resolver still pending full analysis. BSS default string is auto; CompressionFieldParams default contains no chosen BSS mode. (rust/lance-encoding/src/constants.rs:9-65; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:6381-6392; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:55-73)

### Memory ownership and row accounting

AccumulationQueue tracks Arrow-reported memory and caller-supplied top-level row counts. insert flushes only above the budget, includes the overshooting array and keeps that triggering array without copying. Retained arrays at/below budget are copied unless keep_original_array is set. The queue is synchronous and holds exclusive mutable state; callers separately synchronize rep/def builders. Row order/count validity and avoidance of the u64::MAX first-row sentinel collision are caller obligations. (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs:10-105; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7974-8005)

BytepackedIntegerEncoder stores 1/2/4/8-byte LE integers selected from declared maximum. Zero omits every appended value and carries no count. Checked append validates storage width, not the original maximum; trusted append has debug assertions only. ByteUnpacker requires external width1/2/4/8 and panics on an incomplete last integer; there is no zero-width decoder. Full-zip deliberately uses the Zero mode to omit repetition indices when repetition is absent. (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/bytepack.rs:73-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:6555-6607)

### Codec extension seam and errors

BufferCompressor is Debug+Send+Sync with compress/decompress/config. GeneralBufferCompressor creates feature-gated Zstd or LZ4 implementations, or a no-op copier; FSST is rejected because it has a separate path. Zstd initializes a reusable compression context lazily in OnceLock<Result<Mutex<_>,String>>: failure is cached and poisoning can panic. Compression is serialized on that mutex, while decompression creates no shared context here. Every implementation appends to output; failures after resizing/appending do not roll it back. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:141-576)

CompressionConfig::default is always Lz4,Some(0). CompressedBufferEncoder::default instead chooses Zstd,Some(0), otherwise Lz4,None, otherwise None,None according to features. A no-op buffer codec can work yet fail to build structural General metadata because pb21 conversion permits only LZ4/Zstd. A feature-disabled request returns an explicit InvalidInput; a Zstd factory success may still fail at lazy context initialization. These defaults and errors are distinct API contracts. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:65-110; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:200-217; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:538-653; rust/lance-encoding/src/format.rs:406-431)

Whole-block compression preserves selected configuration, including level presence, in the descriptor. Per-value compression uses runtime config, which normalizes absent Zstd level to Some(0) and discards LZ4 level. GeneralBlockDecompressor composes any recursively selected inner decoder; CompressedBufferEncoder's own BlockDecompressor always delegates to BinaryBlockDecompressor and is only the variable-block convenience path. Do not decode arbitrary fixed-width output with that convenience implementation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:577-819; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1335-1353)

Per-value helpers require valid monotone in-bounds offsets and representable cumulative output offsets. They append into caller storage but start the returned offsets at zero, so ordinary standalone output requires an initially empty destination. Unsupported bit widths panic in typed adapters. No file IO, async cancellation, allocation cap or numeric version check is implemented by these codecs. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:656-821)

public; function.

```rust
pub fn get_field_params(         &self,         field_name: &str,         data_type: &DataType,     ) -> CompressionFieldParams {
```

get_field_params borrows config, field name and DataType, creates default params, renders data_type.to_string() for exact type-key lookup and merges that record first. The exact display spelling matters. An exact columns key then merges and prevents the wildcard branch, even if the record has no Some fields. Without an exact key, scan columns in HashMap iteration order, merge the first matching pattern and break. No sorting, specificity scoring or combination of several patterns. Overlapping wildcard results therefore have no stable precedence contract. Return owned merged record; input config is not mutated. ### lance_encoding::compression_config::matches_pattern

private; function.

```rust
fn matches_pattern(name: &str, pattern: &str) -> bool {
```

Private matches_pattern(name,pattern)->bool: exact * matches all; otherwise trailing * branch wins and uses literal prefix before one final star; otherwise leading * uses literal suffix after one first star; otherwise split at first embedded * and require prefix,suffix and name.len()>=pattern.len()-1; otherwise exact equality. Lengths are UTF-8 bytes. This is not a general glob: *foo* requires a literal *foo prefix; further stars remain literal. Empty expansion is possible; middle length guard prevents prefix/suffix overlap such as test_name matching test_*_name. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression_config.rs:143-170)


Public flush returns None for empty buffer with trace and no state reset in that branch. Otherwise trace, save first row/count, reset bytes/sentinel/rows and take vector. Repeated successful drain then flush yields None. No automatic flush-on-drop, local tests, unsafe blocks, async lifecycle or locking. ### lance_encoding::utils::accumulation::AccumulationQueue::insert

public; function.

```rust
pub fn insert(         &mut self,         array: ArrayRef,         row_number: u64,         num_rows: u64,     ) -> Option<(Vec<ArrayRef>, u64, u64)> {
```

Public insert owns ArrayRef and accepts row_number,num_rows; returns Option<(Vec<ArrayRef>,u64,u64)>. If sentinel, set first row; add supplied row count and array.get_array_memory_size() as u64. Ordinary additions can overflow; no ordering, contiguity, length or count validation. A legitimate first row u64::MAX collides with the sentinel. Accounting precedes copying and reflects Arrow-reported memory, not a strict serialized-byte budget. When current_bytes>cache_bytes (strict greater), log and append triggering array without copying even when keep_original_array=false. Save first-row/count, reset bytes/sentinel/rows, mem::take all arrays and return Some. Thus returned group includes the overshooting array; no array splitting or hard memory cap. Input order is preserved. At or below budget, trace and either retain original handle or deep-copy through lance_arrow, then push and return None. No Result/rollback mechanism; a panic during copy occurs after counters changed. Contextual deep_copy_array builds from recursively copied ArrayData with preserved type,length,offset and nulls; its safety relies on valid input ArrayData, not validation in this queue. (rust/lance-arrow/src/deepcopy.rs:35-77) (rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs:37-49; rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs:50-66; rust/lance-encoding/src/utils/accumulation.rs:67-80)

## Buffer ownership, chunk framing and general mini-block composition

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs.md): Public Arrow-backed owned byte-buffer abstraction, typed views, byte slicing, concatenation, raw-pointer interleaving and owned iteration. Alignment, ownership and unsafe preconditions are separate contracts.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs.md): Full-zip value-compression extension trait and fixed/variable owned result union; no concrete compression or file-version dispatch.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs.md): Parent-module-visible lazy automatic sparse-candidate selector. Eligibility is based on an optional explicit setting and dense rep/def budget, not directly on format version.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs.md): Mini-block page/chunk records, owned compression trait and process-wide maximum-value policy. Records describe framing but do not enforce their invariants.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs.md): Metadata-only constant/all-null decompressor with distinct whole-block and fixed-per-value input contracts.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs.md): Outer general-purpose compression of the first mini-block buffer, accepted only for an aggregate size improvement; decoder unwraps that first buffer before inner dispatch.

### Buffer ownership and unsafe preconditions

LanceBuffer owns Arrow Buffer storage. Consuming conversion, cloning and valid byte slicing preserve shared ownership; deep_copy and ordinary concat allocate/copy. concat_into_one preserves a singleton allocation. reinterpret_vec preserves the typed allocation through Arrow; reinterpret_slice retains Arc ownership through custom allocation. No conversion byte-swaps; the crate rejects big-endian targets. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:12-60; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:111-142; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:205-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:283-295; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:11-16)

borrow_to_typed_slice returns an owning ScalarBuffer, sharing only when aligned. borrow_to_typed_view returns Cow, borrowing only when aligned and otherwise copying. Both panic on nondivisible byte lengths. from_bytes conditionally copies on misalignment, but its Vec<u8> branch does not explicitly request the supplied alignment; typed access checks again. Width0 is not rejected and reaches problematic arithmetic/alignment. as_spaced_hex(0) divides by zero. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:62-109; rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:144-203; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:8-17)

zip_into_one is a safe API containing unchecked raw copies. It validates bit-width divisibility by8, but not source length, sums, multiplication or usize conversion. Correct execution requires every buffer contain at least num_values*width bytes and all arithmetic/addressing fit. Malformed inputs can produce out-of-bounds raw access; this is a source-derived safety finding, not a reproduced failure. Its older packed-struct caller only debug-checks equal field counts in the inspected slice. Do not extend that frozen path while designing new format features. (rust/lance-encoding/src/buffer.rs:226-260; rust/lance-encoding/src/array_encoding/physical/packed_struct.rs:172-249; AGENTS.md:15-20)

### Chunk representation and layout selection

PerValueCompressor promises independent value decoding and returns Fixed or Variable data plus descriptor; variable size includes offsets. MiniBlockCompressor promises chunk-level decoding, nonfinal power-of-two counts and owned parallel buffers. These traits/records do not enforce metadata/data agreement. MiniBlockChunk log0 means total minus previous; otherwise1<<log, with unchecked subtraction/shift and no final-position check. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/fullzip.rs:20-54; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:221-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:979-982; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:45-156)

MAX_MINIBLOCK_BYTES=8186 concerns value data. LANCE_MINIBLOCK_MAX_VALUES defaults4096, accepts integer input then clamps1..32768 and is cached once by LazyLock. Non-power-of-two inputs are retained. Rep/def budgeting separately computes min(131072/bits_per_level,65535); zero is invalid and huge widths can yield0. The private fields of MiniBlockCompressionContext are stored by new but repository lexical search found no field reads, so their names are not evidence of active enforcement. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-90; [lexical reference inventory](../analysis/iteration-073-lexical-use-sites.json))

Automatic sparse selection is lazy: any explicit setting suppresses it; only RequiresPageSplit or SingleRowOverBudget invokes the candidate. WithinBudget avoids work. The helper has no format-version argument: v2.2 composition installs rejection and dense_u32; v2.3 installs sparse planning then constant and dense_u32. Sparse planning returns dense fallback for unsupported values or preparation errors; planning errors still propagate. Explicit sparse follows a separate branch. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/layout.rs:8-24; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/mod.rs:121-131; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/mod.rs:129-139; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:7802-7876)

### Metadata-only and outer-compression decode

ConstantDecompressor whole-block mode requires absent payload, including rejecting Some(empty); scalarNone returns AllNull and scalarSome returns compact Constant with caller count. Fixed-per-value mode ignores the supplied block and uses the separate count. Some(empty) is distinct from None despite both reporting width0. These outputs do not allocate one scalar copy per value. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/constant.rs:158-206; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:980-1006)

GeneralMiniBlockCompressor first runs inner compression, then skips outer work when there is no buffer or first-buffer length<4096. Otherwise it compresses each first-buffer chunk independently; only aggregate strict savings are accepted. Remaining buffers move unchanged, sizes[0] are rewritten, count/logs retained and selected configuration wraps inner metadata. Missing sizes, invalid slices or arithmetic overflow are not converted to validation errors. Factory/config failures may be hidden by early fallback. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs:93-188)

GeneralMiniBlockDecompressor reconstructs the outer codec on each call, expands buffer0 and delegates with all remaining buffers and unchanged count. It expects an already separated chunk; the enclosing descriptor strategy recursively creates the inner decoder. decoded_size_bytes delegates to inner. Codec feature availability remains a factory-time concern; neither wrapper constructor validates it. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/general.rs:190-229; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1133-1154; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:538-576)

### lance_encoding::buffer::LanceBuffer::zip_into_one

public; function.

```rust
pub fn zip_into_one(buffers: Vec<(Self, u64)>, num_values: u64) -> Result<Self> {
```

zip_into_one consumes buffers paired with bit widths and a u64 value count. It rejects widths not divisible by8 with InvalidInput including the width; zero width is accepted. Computes per-buffer byte widths, unchecked sum and product, casts total and widths to usize, allocates zeroed output, and retains all input owners while collecting raw pointers. No validation of source length versus num_values*width, integer representability or output arithmetic. Unsafe zipper loops until output pointer reaches end, copies each source width with copy_nonoverlapping and advances both pointers. For valid inputs it interleaves rows in supplied buffer order and ignores surplus source tails. Safety requires each source contain every requested value and all size/address arithmetic fit; these are not established by this safe public function. Short inputs or overflow can cause out-of-bounds raw access, not merely a Result error. No unsafe probe was executed. Empty buffers, zero rows or all-zero widths produce empty output. Independent output allocation supplies nonoverlap for valid sources. No local SAFETY justification accompanies this block. A lexical production caller is the older packed-struct encoder; it derives count from first field and checks equal counts only with debug_assert, without establishing byte lengths in the inspected snippet. Preserve its frozen legacy boundary. fn compress(         &self,         context: MiniBlockCompressionContext,         page: DataBlock,     ) -> Result<(MiniBlockCompressed, CompressiveEncoding)> {

Private MIN_BUFFER_SIZE_FOR_COMPRESSION=4096 bytes. compress first delegates owned page and unchanged context to inner. If data is empty or first whole buffer length<4096, return inner result and descriptor unchanged before factory validation. Equality attempts compression. Threshold is aggregate first-buffer size, not each chunk or sum of all buffers. Inner errors propagate. After threshold, obtain one outer codec for the page or return its error. For each inner chunk index buffer_sizes[0], slice first data buffer by cumulative offset, append compressed chunk bytes, compute output length delta asu32, clone size vector and replace only element0 while preserving log count. Missing first size or invalid range panics; arithmetic and narrowing are unchecked. Assumes chunk sizes exactly cover first input buffer; accepted path drops any unaccounted trailing bytes. Other buffers are not compressed. Context flags are passed inward but not used to revalidate compressed sizes. If summed compressed bytes>=summed original chunk bytes, discard scratch data/chunks and return original result/descriptor. Equality and zero total fall back. Acceptance is strict aggregate savings; one chunk may grow if others compensate. Trace ratio is f32 diagnostic only. Work and temporary memory have already been spent before fallback. On acceptance replace buffer0 with compressed bytes, move all remaining original buffers unchanged, preserve num_values and store rewritten chunk sizes. Wrap selected CompressionConfig around the original encoding using ProtobufUtils21::wrapped; descriptor conversion may error after compression. Retains selected optional level rather than runtime-normalized codec config. Page input, compressed scratch and cloned metadata coexist during work; no strict allocation cap. Noop typically falls back for equal size; unsupported factory config may remain unobserved on small pages. ## Raw values, fixed-size lists and bitpacking

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs.md): Raw fixed-width and nested fixed-size-list encoding/decompression for block, mini-block and per-value interfaces. Each interface has different buffer/count/validity conventions; this file is synchronous and does not perform IO or select exact file versions.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/bitpacking.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/bitpacking.rs.md): Inline per-chunk native-width headers and out-of-line fixed-width FastLanes block compression/decompression. Explicit framing, raw-tail heuristic, allocation and unchecked kernel contracts are distinct from high-level selection.

### Raw values and fixed-size lists

ValueEncoder implements three distinct interfaces. Block compression accepts FixedWidth only and returns its unchanged buffer as Some, including empty buffers. Mini-block compression handles FixedWidth and nested FSL, with parallel validity buffers followed by the unchanged leaf buffer. Per-value compression handles FixedWidth or FSL; nullable FSL is copied into row-major validity bytes followed by leaf bytes, while nonnullable FSL moves its leaf storage. None of these paths performs IO. Invalid input handling differs: block/mini-block unsupported variants return errors, while per-value unsupported variants panic. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:151-309; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:350-494; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:854-869)

Raw mini-block selection starts with two byte-aligned values, or eight nonaligned values using an estimated sixteen-value size. It doubles while estimated bytes remain strictly below 8186 and doubled count stays within the cached maximum. Initial count can already exceed a small configured maximum. Zero width reaches a debug assertion; malformed byte/count relationships are not validated. Full chunks retain a positive count log even when last; only a residual chunk gets log0. Partial FixedWidth chunks account for all remaining bytes, not a recomputed logical byte count. The comment's 4KiB bound is not the actual 8186-byte constant. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:30-115; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-34)

Mini-block FSL preserves whole outer rows. Cumulative dimensions scale each child validity bit slice and leaf size; buffers are ordered outer validity through inner validity, then leaf data. Nullable leaf AllNull is unsupported here, unlike the per-value route. Per-row validity estimates can overestimate actual chunk-wide bitmap bytes; initial validity-vector capacity omits rows-per-chunk and can grow despite the preallocation comment. Dimension products, slicing and several casts remain unchecked. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:141-309)

Per-value FSL descriptors use every actual dimension. However simple_per_value_fsl repeatedly multiplies by the original outer dimension. For a nonnullable outer dimension2, inner dimension3 and 32-bit leaf, its block reports128 bits per row while its descriptor implies192. This follows directly from source arithmetic; no Lance runtime reproduction was run. Recursive is_nullable sends nullable descendants to the separate helper, which does multiply actual dimensions. Equal-dimension direct tests and nullable randomized tests do not establish coverage of the discrepant nonnullable case. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:323-396; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:449-455; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:1072-1102; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:1350-1429; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1291-1302)

Nullable per-value FSL allocates ceil(cumulative_dimension/8) validity bytes per nullable layer per outer row. Its leaf stride is ceil(leaf_bits/8)*dimension_product, requiring byte-expanded leaf items on this route. Direct bitpacked Boolean input does not satisfy this assumption; the complete caller normalization trace remains pending. AllNull synthesizes zero validity and no leaf bytes. Descriptor parsing treats any Constant terminal as width0, even scalarSome. On unzip, width0 becomes AllNull; the simple route instead returns a width0 FixedWidth leaf. Decoder entry point therefore matters. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:363-447; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:525-594; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:719-828)

ValueDecompressor::from_flat copies width without validating optional compression. from_fsl accumulates actual dimensions and row validity bytes, rejecting missing values/compression and unsupported terminals. Block decode requires Some payload and returns a flat leaf block even if constructed from FSL metadata. Mini-block decode pops buffers in reverse, reconstructs child validity and FSL, panics on missing buffers, and ignores unused leading buffers. Per-value unzip asserts byte-aligned leaf and exact total length, discards per-row validity padding and reconstructs layers. Size estimation is None with validity; otherwise checked count*row_bits rounded up to bytes. These estimates exclude allocation capacity and validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:516-852)

### Bitpacking contracts and selection

The current bitpacking module is gated by feature bitpacking. It supports unsigned native widths8/16/32/64 and 1024-value FastLanes chunks. Constructors do not validate widths. Inline min_size_bytes is 128*compressed_width and excludes its native-width header; the policy's full mini-block estimator includes headers, whereas the small block check uses this header-excluding helper. Selection needs statistics populated in BlockInfo; get_stat panics when absent. max_bit_widths derives widths by unsigned OR per physical chunk, so signed negative bit patterns usually prevent savings. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical.rs:10-11; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/bitpacking.rs:39-99; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:339-457; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:129-177; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:315-341; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:353-406)

Inline encoding prefixes each chunk with compressed width stored as one uncompressed native word, then writes the packed 1024-value payload. The final chunk is padded with zeros, always has log0, and still contains a full packed payload. Width0 is header-only. The encoder trusts supplied per-chunk statistics and data shape; wrong small widths lose high bits through kernel masking. Unsafe writes target reserved uninitialized capacity and set length after kernel initialization. Kernel assertions demand exact input/output word counts. These are preconditions of the fast path, not malformed-input validation. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/bitpacking.rs:106-218; rust/compression/bitpacking/src/lib.rs:74-174; rust/compression/bitpacking/src/lib.rs:175-278)

Inline positive-count decode checks native header length, native-word divisibility, count<=1024, width<=native width and exact packed payload length before invoking the unsafe kernel. Failures are CorruptFile errors with inline_bitpacking context. It allocates1024 values, unpacks and truncates; padding is not checked for zero, capacity remains1024. Mini-block decode asserts exactly one buffer even for count0; whole-block decode requires Some even for count0. Private generic bitpack_out_of_line borrows full typed payload and derives number of chunks/remainder from physical typed length, ignoring FixedWidthDataBlock.num_values. Compute ceil(1024*W/data.bits_per_value) native output words; allocate num_chunks*words capacity. If widths/counts/arithmetic are malformed, no Result validation here. For tail R, compute savings=(T-W).saturating_sub semantics through T.saturating_sub(W), padding_cost=W*(1024-R), tail_savings=saturating((T-W)*R); debug-assert R>0 and positive savings. Pack a zero-padded1024 tail only if padding_cost<tail_savings; equality uses raw T values. This is equivalent to comparing packed1024W with rawRT for valid arithmetic. Raw append may reallocate; padded tail uses reserved words. W>=T on a runt tail violates debug assertion even though constructor accepts it. No tail marker is written. ### lance_encoding::encodings::physical::bitpacking::unpack_out_of_line

private; function; feature=bitpacking.

```rust
fn unpack_out_of_line<T: ArrowNativeType + BitPackingUninit>(     data: FixedWidthDataBlock,     num_values: usize,     compressed_bits_per_value: usize, ) -> FixedWidthDataBlock {
```

unpack_out_of_line computes words per chunk from W and supplied native-width field, obtains typed compressed slice, and derives full/tail counts from requested num_values. Raw tail recognized only when R>0 and total compressed word count==full_words+R; otherwise assume padded packed tail. This length rule is essential at equal-size tie because raw native layout differs from FastLanes transpose. Allocate num_values.saturating_add(1024) T capacity. Arithmetic before allocation remains largely unchecked. Unsafe-unpack each full chunk from bounds-checked slice into1024 spare outputs, set_len afterward. Raw tail copies R words; packed tail reads one packed chunk, decodes1024 and truncates to R. Debug output length equality, then FixedWidth with original native-width field/requested count/fresh stats. No exact total-payload length validation, no padded-tail-zero check: too-short slices panic; surplus words can be ignored or alter raw-vs-packed classification. Zero requested values allocates capacity1024 and ignores all typed input after divisibility conversion. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/bitpacking.rs:495-518; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/bitpacking.rs:519-565)

## Variable, FSST and byte-stream-split codecs

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs.md): Current variable-width mini-block, block and per-value encoders/decoders, offset validation and tests. No IO or local unsafe; the block decoder retains a frozen old-header read branch.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/fsst.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/fsst.rs.md): Current FSST wrappers for variable mini-block and per-value data; delegates symbol-table kernel and inner codec, owns allocation/metadata/error mapping. Kernel crate remains partially analyzed.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/byte_stream_split.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/byte_stream_split.rs.md): Byte-position transposition of32/64-bit fixed values within mini-block chunks, inverse, entropy selector and three unit tests. Transform preserves length and relies on separate compression.

### Variable-width interfaces and validation

Binary mini-blocks encode their own offset table at the beginning of each chunk, using signed32/64-bit input offsets rebased to chunk start plus table bytes. Each chunk is padded with0x48 to4/8-byte alignment respectively. The output is one concatenated buffer plus external chunk descriptors; logical num_values is retained from input even though chunk partitioning uses offsets.len()-1. Per-value VariableEncoder and VariableDecoder instead move an existing VariableWidthBlock unchanged. Whole-block VariableEncoder writes a separate width/data-start header, then original offsets and all original value bytes. These interfaces are not interchangeable. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:89-183; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:402-527; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:879-992)

The binary chunk target defaults4096 bytes via cached LANCE_BINARY_MINIBLOCK_CHUNK_SIZE; unparsable values fall back, parsed zero/negative values remain accepted. Chunk search starts at two values, grows by powers of two and treats final-tail fitting separately. The target is not a hard bound; alignment follows estimation, the initial two may exceed it, and the tail-fit branch bypasses MAX_MINIBLOCK_VALUES. The normal branch checks doubled candidate against the cap before accepting candidate, so cap4096 can stop at2048. new(Some(...)) still evaluates the lazy default because unwrap_or is eager. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:39-61; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:189-508)

Mini decode asserts one buffer, checks native-word divisibility/table capacity, first offset>=requested table bytes, monotonicity and last<=chunk bytes, then copies rebased offsets and selected payload. First need not equal the requested table size, allowing a requested prefix of a larger chunk. It does not validate UTF-8 or unrequested offsets. new asserts32/64, whereas from_variable directly casts a nested Flat width to u8; malformed width can reach division by zero or the fallback32 branch. Normal strategy calls new, but first narrows metadata to u8 too. This is source-derived behavior, not an executed malformed-input reproduction. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:547-876; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1061-1070)

Whole-block decode validates header, checked external offset count/size, exact offset-region length and first offset zero, then returns shared buffer slices. Remaining monotonicity/bounds/UTF-8 checks are deferred until mandatory Arrow conversion, even if the internal caller passes validate=false. Arrow validation requires the right offset width and at least the required offset bytes, handles signed offsets, verifies visible payload bounds and, for strings, joined visible UTF-8 plus each offset boundary. Only then does it use unchecked Arrow construction. Binary direct decode success is therefore a weaker contract than Arrow validity. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/binary.rs:998-1149; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:742-969; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1193-1234)

### FSST wrappers, kernel and selection

FSST compression accepts VariableWidth32/64, allocates twice input byte length, twice offset ELEMENT count and a2312-byte table, then delegates to the local fsst crate. No local benefit check or normalization. Mini wrapper then invokes BinaryMiniBlockEncoder on compressed bytes; per-value wrapper invokes an injected compressor. Decode first runs inner decoding, allocates eight times compressed byte length and offset entries, invokes the kernel, truncates offsets to requested count+1 and resets statistics. Per-value retains inner count, mini uses external count. truncate cannot repair too-short output; wrapper arithmetic is unchecked. Mini non64 width falls through i32 but retains original width; per-value rejects unsupported width by panic. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/fsst.rs:36-392; rust/compression/fsst/src/fsst.rs:22-56)

Decoder InvalidData becomes CorruptFile(named fsst); other IO kinds use ordinary Lance IO conversion. Encode uses ordinary ? conversion directly. Kernel table-size/output-capacity failures are InvalidInput and thus remain IO errors through this mapping; invalid symbol length1..8 or missing escaped byte is InvalidData. Kernel validates nondecreasing in-bounds offsets without requiring first0 or final=data length. Small-input encoding below32768 bytes disables FSST and copies bytes/offsets; metadata still contains a table. Kernel unsafe decode and sampling/table construction are not fully analyzed, so this supplement is not whole-kernel qualification. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/fsst.rs:36-133; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/fsst.rs:215-390; rust/compression/fsst/src/fsst.rs:811-857; rust/compression/fsst/src/fsst.rs:910-1098; rust/compression/fsst/src/fsst.rs:1115-1455)

Mini-block policy validates width and reads data-size/max-length stats before explicit compression=none. Explicit fsst selects FSST; automatic FSST requires no compression parameter, non-Binary/non-LargeBinary type, maximum value length>=5 and data size>=32768. Other named compression wraps raw binary with General compression. Per-value policy checks explicit none before statistics/width; then maxlen>32768 or an explicit non-fsst scheme, together with total size>=32768, selects CompressedBufferEncoder first. Consequently explicit fsst can be overridden by the large-value route. Remaining FSST eligibility matches the mini policy. These are decision-order facts, not compression-ratio guarantees. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:661-736; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:837-881)

Mini FSST reconstruction recursively interprets the nested values descriptor. Per-value FSST reconstruction instead installs VariableDecoder and ignores fsst.values, despite the public encoder allowing a custom inner compressor. A custom inner is not guaranteed to roundtrip through default reconstruction. Variable registrations unwrap Flat metadata and do not apply arbitrary offset compression. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/fsst.rs:171-212; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1061-1134; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1213-1242)

### Byte-stream split and entropy

BSS groups each byte position across values in a single chunk: out[j*n+i]=in[i*width+j]. Width must be configured32/64; chunk caps are1024/512 values, independent of the configurable generic mini-block maximum. Final chunk has log0 even if full. Compression preserves total byte length and needs separate outer compression to save space. The encoder does not compare configured width to DataBlock width or validate physical size; short data panics, trailing data is ignored. Empty encode emits no buffers. Decode count0 returns before buffer validation; positive decode requires exactly one buffer and exact byte count, but does not know chunk maximum. Applying it to concatenated chunks uses the wrong transpose. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/byte_stream_split.rs:79-274)

should_use_bss rejects non32/64 widths, Off returnsfalse and On returnstrue even for empty data. Auto requires average byte-position entropy strictly below4 bits. Missing statistic returnsfalse, but completely empty BlockInfo registry panics in get_stat. Statistics sample the first min(num_values,64) rows, compute per-byte Shannon entropy and truncate entropy*1000 to integers. Missing physical bytes are skipped while sample-count denominator stays fixed. Selector does not verify statistic length/range or Arrow numeric type. The policy additionally requires a compression parameter present and not exactly none, even for BssMode::On; it does not itself validate that codec name in this helper. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/byte_stream_split.rs:277-324; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:311-354; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:500-551; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:154-191)

## Packed structs and statistics

- [rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs.md): Row-major packed structs: fixed mini-block, fixed and variable per-value interfaces, child accumulators and nine local tests. File-version selection belongs to the caller.
- [rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs.md): DataBlock statistic keys, eager/lazy computation, shared cached Arrow arrays, approximate cardinality, bit/run/entropy estimators and ten local tests.

### Packed struct representation and policy

Fixed packing transposes child buffers into row-major bytes. Mini-block packing reads DataSize and all children as FixedWidth, forwards the zipped block to raw ValueEncoder and stores field widths plus nested Flat metadata. Fixed per-value packing validates nonempty/equal-count/direct-fixed children, checked-sums widths and stores raw interleaved bytes. Fixed-size-list and nullable wrappers fail the direct FixedWidth test even if their logical type has fixed size. Mini decode assumes width consistency; fixed per-value decode explicitly checks byte alignment and child-width sum, but accepts surplus bytes and takes external count instead of input block.num_values. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:40-218; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:329-357; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:449-525; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:910-1011; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1044-1048)

Variable packing first compresses each child using the injected strategy. A fixed child contributes configured-width compressed bytes; a variable child contributes u32LE/u64LE compressed length followed by payload. The outer row-offset vector starts0 and selects32bits if total and maximum row size fitu32, otherwise64. Descriptors retain each child codec and fixed-width or length-prefix layout. Decoder copies row offsets, splits every field into builders, then runs each child decoder. It checks offset count, row bounds and exact nonempty-row consumption; it does not require outer first0/final=buffer length. Empty row inserts zero/empty placeholders for every field; no validity bitmap is created locally. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:253-448; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:527-897)

Zero-row variable decode with configured fields reaches DataBlockBuilder::finish without any append and panics. Width0 passes fixed accumulator alignment and multiplication, but the fixed builder's finish divides by zero. Descending encoder child offsets are not explicitly rejected before subtraction/slicing. These are source-derived edge cases, not reproduced runtime failures. Row-by-row temporary block copies, all-offset materialization, and per-variable-field whole-input capacity estimates can increase memory use. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:263-326; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:562-604; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/packed.rs:637-897; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:351-384; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:2078-2123)

Production V2.1 per-value policy rejects packed structs; V2.2 permits variable-packed only; V2.3 uses all-packed helper and adds fixed per-value support. Mini fixed-packed selection is a different helper. Test StructuralU32/StructuralSparse use all-packed selection, so a u32 harness roundtrip does not establish production V2.2 support for fixed full-zip packing. There is no version gate inside packed.rs itself. Stable formats retain their compatibility contracts; these tests do not justify extending frozen legacy code. (rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_1/compression.rs:85-98; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_2/compression.rs:77-93; rust/lance-file/src/versions/v2_3/compression.rs:79-94; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:738-835; rust/lance-encoding/src/testing.rs:162-181; AGENTS.md:5-20)

### Statistics domains and cache lifecycle

ComputeStat has no Result and GetStat can panic for uninitialized maps. Fixed blocks eagerly populate DataSize, BitWidth, MaxLength, RunCount and BytePositionEntropy; variable blocks populate DataSize/MaxLength exactly once according to a non-atomic empty-map check. Cardinality is lazy, supported for variable data and fixed64/128 only. BlockInfo is a cloneable Arc<RwLock<HashMap<Stat,Arc<dyn Array>>>>; calculation occurs outside locks and entry-or-insert caches the first result. Fixed recomputation overwrites eager keys without clearing a prior cardinality. Do not assume cloned statistics remain valid after mutating one block's payload. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:52-216; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:324-350; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:63-85)

Statistics use different domains. BitWidth scans all physical unsigned8/16/32/64 words in1024-value chunks, except declared count0 returns[0]. RunCount scans all physical8/16/32/64/128 words, except declared count0 returns0; unsupported widths return declared count. Cardinality hashes all offset windows or fixed words with HLL precision4: variable and64-bit use xxhash,128-bit uses RandomState. Entropy samples only the first min(declared count,64) values and emits floor(bits/8) entries of Shannon entropy*1000 truncated to u64. Missing sample bytes are skipped but denominator unchanged. These values are not interchangeable measures of logical valid rows. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:232-308; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:353-549)

Nullable forwards stats without null filtering; AllNull supplies only DataSize0 and NullCount. Dictionary supplies no stats. FixedSizeList forwards child stats except multiplying MaxLength by dimension. Struct requires precomputed scalar child MaxLength and sums it without computing children; unsupported child MaxLength panics. FixedSize is a declared key with no producer in this file. Generic expect_single_stat checks array type/length but does not check scalar validity. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:19-29; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:140-186; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:217-229; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:311-321; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:552-594)


Byte-position entropy samples first min(num_values-as-usize,64) declared values using local SAMPLE_SIZE=64. Zero sample gives empty UInt64Array. For each floor(bits/8) byte position, count occurrences in256 u32 counters; missing physical positions are skipped rather than errors. One-bit boolean width has zero byte positions. For each byte position compute Shannon -sum(p*log2(p)), dividing each count by declared sample count even if bytes were missing; multiply1000 and castu64. (rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:282-310)

Callees: Observed lexical call expressions (not a resolved call graph): .borrow_to_typed_slice, .as_ref, .windows, .map, .max, .unwrap_or, Arc::new, UInt64Array::from.


## Compression policy and dispatch — cycle77

[Complete file analysis](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs.md), [symbol index](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md), [behavior contracts](../L3-symbols/behavior-contracts.md) and [development recipes](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md).

### Shared compression selection and decoder dispatch

The public CompressionStrategy has separate block, per-value and mini-block factories. DefaultDecompressionStrategy implements the four read factories, but there is no default writer strategy in this module: production lance-file versions compose public selector helpers. None payload and Some(empty) are different states; compress_required_block rejects metadata-only output, while reader traits expose requires_payload and optional count inference. Exact decoded-size hooks are optional and default to None. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:92-158; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:936-1033)

RLE selection accepts native widths8/16/32/64 and initialized RunCount. Only an explicitly supplied ratio threshold imposes runs<count*threshold; the named0.5 constant does not impose an automatic cutoff. Payload must be strictly smaller than raw, including an8-byte header for whole blocks; ties with a bitpacking estimate favor RLE. Mini estimators suppress errors into fallback, block estimators propagate them. Adaptive mini selection can trial-compress child streams when its initial estimate would lose; this can repeat work during actual encoding. Inline estimates pad each statistic segment to1024 values; out-of-line runt estimates choose raw tail on equal padding/savings cost. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:180-516; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1013-1039)

Metadata parsing is permissive: unknown compression strings remain strings; invalid numeric level/threshold parses become None, invalid BSS/minichunk parses warn, and signed/nonfinite parsed values receive no semantic validation here. Explicit codec settings have interface-specific behavior. Variable mini selection validates offsets and stats before the none shortcut, chooses FSST only explicitly or automatically for eligible nonbinary fields, and wraps explicit other codecs. Variable per-value none bypasses stats/offset validation; on sufficiently large payloads exact zstd honors its level but other explicit non-FSST strings select the feature-dependent default encoder. Small explicit general requests fall back raw without parsing. Whole-block automatic general compression uses physical size strictly greater than32768, whereas the per-value data threshold is inclusive. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:532-591; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:662-736; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:839-880; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/block.rs:615-633)

Default decoder dispatch is interface-specific:

| Interface | Supported descriptors | Unsupported behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Mini | Flat, InlineBitpacking with feature, Variable, FSST, PackedStruct, FSL, RLE, BSS, General | VariablePackedStruct returns NotSupported; other unhandled tags panic via todo; Inline without feature returns NotSupported. |
| Fixed per-value | Constant, Flat, FSL, PackedStruct | Other tags panic. |
| Variable per-value | Variable, FSST, General, VariablePackedStruct | Other tags panic. |
| Block | InlineBitpacking, Flat, Constant, Variable, FSL, OutOfLineBitpacking, General, RLE | Other tags panic. |

All four unwrap missing outer compression. Inner descriptors mix explicit InvalidInput with unwrap/assert/panic assumptions. Variable per-value FSST hardcodes its raw inner reader; General ignores values/level for read; block Variable uses its payload header instead of nested descriptor contents. Mini FSST and RLE route through the supplied nested strategy, but General recurses via self while carrying that strategy onward. There is no local file-version or recursion-depth gate. Block bitpacking references are ungated despite feature-gated imports: potential no-bitpacking build failure inferred from source, not compiled. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:19-80; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:427-454; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1034-1372)

RLE children permit Flat, OutOfLineBitpacking->Flat, General->Flat, or General->OutOfLineBitpacking->Flat. The grammar excludes Inline, nested General, Constant and other tags before custom reader dispatch. Value width must be8/16/32/64; length width8/16/32. Out-of-line children require run count; both children may not require it, because decoding needs an independently inferable count. Child readers are constructed before final width/dependency validation, so their errors may take precedence. Both direct Flat children use identity/raw RLE. (rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:1757-1928; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1195-1213)

## Physical RLE — cycle78

[Complete file and source evidence](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs.md), [declarations](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md), [format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md), [recipes](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md).

### Physical RLE: writing, child selection and reading

Public RleEncoder::new uses U8 literal run lengths and raw children. Crate-internal constructors can choose U16/U32 lengths and mini child compression. Public RleDecompressor::new(value_bits) likewise uses raw U8 lengths. Constructors retain unchecked settings; shared strategy validation is a separate boundary. These codecs perform no IO, async work, mutation of shared state or local unsafe operation. Native value bytes rely on the crate little-endian guard. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:56-141; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:329-384; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1152-1312; rust/lance-encoding/src/lib.rs:27-31)

Each physical entry consists of one native unsigned value bit pattern and its positive literal repeat count. Signed integers and floats therefore group by bits, not arithmetic comparison. A run exceeding255/65535/4294967295 splits into repeated entries at the selected width. Adjacent physical entries can have equal values. Width cost uses entry_count*(value_bytes+length_bytes), with narrower widths winning ties; headers, child codecs and structural framing are excluded. Per-run segment estimation does not model aligned mini boundaries or the byte budget exactly. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:76-328; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:636-725)

| Contract | Mini writer/reader | Whole-block writer/reader |
|---|---|---|
| Input shape | Direct FixedWidth; zero count returns before byte/width validation. Nonzero bytes are visited as a prefix; surplus bytes can be ignored and short/misaligned bytes may error or panic. | Direct FixedWidth; checks native width, count conversion, checked byte size and exact input length even for zero count. |
| Framing | Two global child buffers plus per-chunk sizes/logical-count logs; outer mini framing belongs to the structural layer. | Present payload with an eight-byte LE values-byte-size header, values bytes, then all length bytes; empty output is eight zero bytes. |
| Chunking | Raw payload must fit8186 bytes and configured value cap; nonfinal chunks are powers of two greater than one, final log is zero. | No mini chunk boundaries; only run-width splitting. |
| Child compression | Flat, optional General and optional feature-gated OutOfLineBitpacking candidates. | Always raw Flat children, regardless of configured child settings. |
| Overflow | Eager expansion clamps the run that crosses expected logical count and stops. | Eager expansion rejects overflow. |
| Empty read | Count zero ignores children and buffer count. | Frame must parse first, then eager zero-count shortcut applies. Strict lazy RleRuns still validates coverage. |

The table summarizes exact local implementation, not file-version eligibility. Default value cap4096 is lazy environment-controlled by LANCE_MINIBLOCK_MAX_VALUES and clamped1..32768. The module comments claiming2048 and an automatic50% ratio are stale; explicit ratio and cost policy live in shared compression. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:29-55; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:385-634; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1049-1151; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1313-1345; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1533-1713; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive/miniblock.rs:19-34; rust/lance-encoding/src/compression.rs:180-273)

General candidates compress each raw mini chunk separately and retain a concatenation of frames. They must save aggregate bytes, although an individual chunk can expand. Bitpacking chooses one unsigned bit width across the entire child, at least one bit, then packs each chunk separately; it needs the run count from the other child. Selection enumerates candidate pairs, forbids two count-dependent children and minimizes aggregate payload bytes with first-candidate tie preference. Errors while constructing an optional candidate propagate. No second per-chunk byte-budget check follows selection. selected_payload_size actually builds candidates and allocates, so estimation may repeat encoding work. These are source-derived costs and risks, not benchmark results. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:727-1048; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1084-1118)

On read, an independent child is decoded first when the other needs a run count. Run count comes from decoded byte length divided by native width, not infer_num_values. General Flat can return count zero with nonempty bytes; child validation intentionally skips expected-count equality for zero. Outer expansion checks divisibility and equal entry counts, rejects zero lengths and underflow, and reserves the complete expected logical output. Mini overflow ignores later entries only after the overflowing positive run; a zero entry immediately after exact coverage still errors. Whole-block parsing checks the header and section bounds, then child/coverage checks occur. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1215-1276; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1436-1713; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/value.rs:595-613)

Legacy count inference is narrowly limited to value16/lengthU8 with two identity children. It sums validated raw lengths without expansion; all other configurations return None before inspecting the frame. The strict crate-internal decode_u16_runs path instead parses children and requires exact coverage, including expected zero. RleRuns retains physical u16 values and typed lengths, counts adjacent equal runs without merging them, and offers physical iteration. owned_size measures visible bytes, deep_size sums backing capacities, and into_owned copies visible arrays. Primitive lazy levels choose physical/coalesced/dense storage afterward; that caller is not yet fully analyzed. (rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1398-1435; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1658-1672; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/physical/rle.rs:1715-1948; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:1302-1380; rust/lance-encoding/src/encodings/logical/primitive.rs:1796-1800)

## DataBlock — cycle79

[File](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs.md) · [Symbols](../L3-symbols/symbol-index.md) · [Format](../L3-symbols/format-spec.md) · [Recipes](../L4-crosscutting/cookbook.md)

### DataBlock: representation, validity and reconstruction

DataBlock is a public physical representation used between Arrow arrays and encoding strategies. Ten variants carry raw fixed/variable data, validity, fixed lists, structs, dictionary indices/items, constants, all-null or empty values, or opaque encoded buffers. Public fields permit states that constructors do not produce; callers must distinguish fallible checked conversion from infallible normalization and caller-validated helpers. No IO or asynchronous lifecycle occurs here. [Complete analysis](../L2-files/rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs.md). (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1-38; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:40-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:451-661; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:984-1190)

| Operation | Current contract and failure boundary |
|---|---|
| into_arrow(type, validate) | Public flag is ignored and reconstruction always validates. Constant panics; Opaque returns Internal. Fixed-width checked Arrow layout does not separately compare declared physical width with requested type. Boolean physical width8 is repacked. |
| Variable-width Arrow conversion | Requested classic type must match offset width. Nonempty supported types check required offset prefix, monotonicity, nonnegative bounds and string UTF-8/boundaries before one private unchecked build. Zero count and other types use checked Arrow construction. |
| from_arrays(arrays, count) | Public, infallible and does not call validate_arrays. Uses first type and supplied count; zero/empty and all-null shortcuts occur before unsupported-type dispatch. Mismatched counts/types or unsupported non-null nested types can panic or create inconsistent metadata. |
| validate_arrays | Crate-internal pre-encoding boundary: Arrow basic validation plus recursive classic variable-offset checks; InvalidInput includes field and input index. It intentionally avoids a full UTF-8 rescan. |
| into_buffers | Flattens physical buffers without type/count/framing. Nullable validity first, variable offsets first, dictionary indices first; Struct own validity is omitted. |
| try_clone | Infallibly returns Ok, sharing Arrow buffers and BlockInfo maps; stale docs describing owned/borrowed modes do not describe this implementation. |
| data_size | Visible stored bytes, not retained capacity or expanded logical size. Constants count once; Struct parent validity is omitted; shared storage is not deduplicated. |

These contracts follow the dispatch and helper bodies, not just their names. Offset validation accepts nonzero first offsets and unused payload prefixes/suffixes despite normalized-start-zero module documentation; conversion ignores extra offset bytes after the required prefix. Builder append instead requires the whole offsets buffer to be width-divisible. (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:174-224; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:663-982; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:994-1055; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1192-1257; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1342-1356; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1832-2057)

BlockInfo exposes an Arc/RwLock map of statistic arrays. Cloning shares that mutable map; poisoned locks panic through unwrap. Changing public data or using mutable cast accessors does not invalidate statistics. from_arrays computes inner statistics before optional Nullable wrapping; the outer Nullable cache starts empty. Fixed-list flattening retains leaf statistics even when physical width/count change. Struct statistics require child MaxLength values, which may be absent for child kinds that do not compute them. These are source-level preconditions and risks, not reproduced failures. (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:61-86; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:468-514; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1438-1498; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:2027-2044; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:56-71; rust/lance-encoding/src/statistics.rs:579-597)

DataBlockBuilder::with_capacity_estimate is public and initializes no concrete builder. The first append pins shape, even when its validation later fails. Only variable-width append performs its full local offset/range checks; other implementations rely on shape, buffer and dimension preconditions and can panic. Variable append checks capacity overflow before copying, but composite appends are not transactional: child changes can precede later errors, and append_ranges retains prior successful ranges. finish without any initialized builder panics. Struct builder discards parent validity; Nullable builder appends child before validity. The private builder trait is Debug without Send/Sync bounds. (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:226-450; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:542-619; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1374-1435; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:2059-2124)

Dictionary normalization concatenates Arrow dictionaries, promotes overflowing key capacity to UInt32, and represents logical null rows by keys pointing to a null dictionary item. It reuses an existing null item or appends one; indices then have no bitmap. Duplicate dictionary values can remain. Direct dictionary reconstruction verifies declared key width and checked-builds Arrow arrays. Expansion to a non-dictionary type interprets raw keys as unsigned by physical width and iterates the complete physical key buffer, not merely declared index count; empty dictionary/invalid keys and arithmetic overflow remain preconditions. (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1058-1162; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1635-1785; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:2384-2505; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:2523-2555)

Nullability predicates are representation-specific. is_nullable ignores Struct.validity and panics for Dictionary/Opaque; is_variable also does not support those two kinds. remove_outer_validity strips one Nullable layer or recursively clears Struct, but does not recurse into FSL/Dictionary and panics for AllNull. Partial-null Struct conversion can retain both an inner parent bitmap and an outer Nullable bitmap. Fixed-list dimensions are not generally validated; zero dimension or empty Struct count queries can panic. (rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:451-540; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1025-1035; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1274-1340; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1358-1372; rust/lance-encoding/src/data.rs:1978-2044)
